reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that Hf substitution in Fe-Zr-B-Cu alloys enhances magnetocaloric performance (ΔS_M, RCP) and confirms a second-order transition, but it does not provide specific data on interatomic distances, electronic environments, hysteresis, heat exchange rates, or mechanical properties. Thus, only the general link between Hf and improved MCE is supported, while the mechanistic premises about tuning exchange interactions, low hysteresis, rapid heat exchange, and mechanical stability lack direct evidence.
premises: Hf substitution in Fe-Zr-B-Cu alloys tunes interatomic distances and electronic environments
This tuning optimizes magnetic exchange interactions to support a broad, second-order magnetic phase transition
A broad second-order transition yields a strong magnetocaloric response at low applied fields
The broad second-order transition preserves low hysteresis and rapid heat exchange
Mechanical stability is maintained alongside the enhanced magnetocaloric properties
